learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the psychology of buyers! Understand how consumers maximize satisfaction subject to their budget constraints.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Utility is the want-satisfying power of a commodity. The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility states that as you consume more and more units of a good, the extra satisfaction (marginal utility) derived from each successive unit keeps falling.

A curve showing different combinations of two goods that give the consumer equal satisfaction. A consumer is 'indifferent' between any points on this curve. Higher curves mean higher overall satisfaction.
Consumers can't buy everything; they are limited by their income and the prices of goods. The Budget Line shows all combinations of two goods exactly equal to the consumer's income.

The optimal point where the consumer gets maximum satisfaction within their budget. Graphically, it is the exact point where the Budget Line is perfectly tangent to the highest possible Indifference Curve.

fun_activity.title: 🍕 The Pizza Slice Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine eating pizza when you are starving. Slice 1: Absolute heaven (High Marginal Utility). Slice 3: Good, but you're getting full. Slice 6: You feel sick and can't eat another bite (Negative Marginal Utility). This is the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility in real life!

exam_tips: 📌 Remember the relationship: When Marginal Utility (MU) is positive, Total Utility (TU) rises. When MU is zero, TU is at its maximum. When MU becomes negative, TU starts falling.
📌 Properties of Indifference Curves are frequently asked: They slope downward, they are convex to the origin, and two ICs can never intersect each other.
📌 At consumer equilibrium using the ordinal approach, MRS (Marginal Rate of Substitution) = Ratio of Prices (Px/Py).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Law of Demand states that there is an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, keeping other factors constant (Ceteris Paribus).
⭐ Giffen goods are an exception to the law of demand; if their price increases, their demand increases.
⭐ Price elasticity of demand measures how sensitively quantity demanded responds to a change in price.
